# In-flight retired-port errors lack departure identity

## Context

The real #19569 restored-stack return logged `DragZone: proxy removal delta failed` with `PortDisconnectedError` just after its popup closed. A zero-file-change probe at `f502257a3a` independently dispatched a real `WorkerBase.promiseMessage()`, retired its target port and observed the same classification failure. Grace independently verified the emitter and found no open owner.

## The Problem

`removePort()` records the window departure before rejecting pending requests, but the emitted error has only `name: 'PortDisconnectedError'`. Its `code` and `windowId` are absent. The existing shared `isDeparture()` therefore returns false even though the actual target departure is recorded. The unhandled boundary mirrored this rejection once instead of settling it as expected teardown.

A request sent after departure already carries the typed dead-port metadata and classifies correctly. The missing case is a request that was dispatched before the port retired.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: `src/worker/Base.mjs#isDeparture` states “Both halves, always”: `NEO_DEAD_PORT` plus recorded target departure. #19071 established that predicate; its completed scope did not cover this emitter. The merged #19536 / closed #19535 repair handles a specific Workstation repaint consumer by error name, leaving the shared emitter unchanged.

`removePort` owns the pending-request rejection. `DragZone`, `Viewport`, grid/table bodies and other shared-predicate consumers should receive the same existing departure contract. Name-based handlers in `Neo.mjs`, `VdomLifecycle` and `worker/App.mjs` still need the existing error name.

Prescription checked: `src/worker/Base.mjs#removePort` owns the concern. No new consumer predicate or teardown wait is needed.

## The Fix

Add `code: 'NEO_DEAD_PORT'` and the retired port's `windowId` to its in-flight rejection, retaining `PortDisconnectedError` and the existing message. Keep pending-map deletion, exact port-generation ownership and the recorded-departure predicate unchanged.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior / fallback | Docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `WorkerBase.removePort` rejection | Existing typed departure contract / #19071 | In-flight retired-window requests expose code and target identity; error name/message remain compatible. Non-window ports acquire no departure evidence. | Owning JSDoc | Real dispatched window and channel requests, then exact port retirement. |
| `WorkerBase.isDeparture` and unhandled settlement | Existing two-halves JSDoc | Recorded target departure settles silently; ordinary, unknown or foreign-window failures remain visible. Predicate unchanged. | Existing JSDoc | Actual emitted reason plus negative controls and unhandled-boundary observation. |
| Generation fencing | Existing `ReplyLoss` contract | A retired/foreign port does not reject a successor request or admit its stale reply. | Existing source | Existing successor tests and focused regression. |

Decision Record impact: none — restores the existing transport terminal; no new architecture or configuration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A real in-flight window request rejected by `removePort` carries the existing error name/message, `NEO_DEAD_PORT`, and exact target window ID; its pending entry is deleted.
- [ ] The same holds for an in-flight channel request routed through that window; a non-window port remains a non-departure.
- [ ] The actual emitted reason satisfies the existing two-halves predicate and settles at the unhandled boundary. Ordinary and foreign-window failures remain observable.
- [ ] Successor-port request/reply isolation remains intact. Owning worker tests and a real `DragZone` cleanup consumer control cover the repair.

## Out of Scope

No broad suppression by error name, new waits, changed departure retention, consumer predicate proliferation, or retirement-policy change. The film choreography and headed placement remain #19569. No hosted quarantine is retired under this ticket.
